item.title: Intermolecular decoupling of C<sub>60</sub> suppresses interfacial recombination in perovskite solar cells
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02030-x Interfacial recombination in perovskite solar cells is mitigated through a vapour-phase molecular passivation method using trialkylamines, disrupting C60 packing. item.title: A highway instead of a racetrack: Strong coupling of light and sound in an optical fiber
item.description: For the first time, scientists have achieved strong coupling between light and long-lived acoustic vibrations in an optical fiber. Optical fibers are used in both classical telecommunications and quantum communication and could serve not only as connections between computing nodes but also as quantum processors themselves in the future. The results, published in Nature Physics, pave the way for new technologies in quantum signal processing.

item.description: Magnetic skyrmions (MSks) are swirling patterns of magnetization that form inside certain magnetic materials. They can behave like actual particles in many ways, exhibiting a stable internal structure and distinct boundaries. Because they are extremely small and can be pushed around with relatively little energy, MSks are regarded as promising information carriers in emerging technologies, including low-power memories and logic circuits.
